processing: Fully oxidised black tea; local details are not documented here.
harvest_season: Spring and summer pickings, as is usual for Kagoshima black tea.
appearance_dry: Dark, twisted leaf, as is typical of Japanese black tea.
taste_profile: Little is documented about this tea; Kagoshima black teas are typically soft and sweet rather than very astringent.
vintage_note: Sold as the current year's harvest in small lots; it is not usually aged.
description:
Makurazaki is a port town at the southern tip of Kagoshima Prefecture, and Makurazaki koucha is a black tea named after it. Kagoshima is Japan's second largest tea region and has a warm climate.

Very little is documented about this particular tea, so no specific cultivar or flavour is claimed here. Typically, Japanese black tea is made by withering, rolling, oxidising and drying the leaf.

If you come across it, ask the seller for the cultivar and the pick date; those two facts tell you most about the cup.
history: Makurazaki black tea appears in lists of local Japanese black teas of Kagoshima Prefecture alongside Kagoshima and Akune black tea. Its origins and dates are not documented here.
